edits_applied.before: Among the retainers was Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, and once the guests were seated, he went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then stopped the carriage on the way to call on a butcher friend, and stood about a long time in the marketplace so that passers-by would stare; Wuji's manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he was a mere gatekeeper, and the prince had personally come for him before a crowd — a kindness he could not let pass without repaying. "I wanted to make your name," he said, "so I stood a long time by your carriage in the market while people watched, and the more I tried you, the more respectful you became. The townsfolk took me for a lout and you for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars." When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became Wuji's chief retainer.

edits_applied.before: Wuji's reputation rested on his habit of humbling himself before men of talent: humane and courteous to scholars whether able or not, never letting wealth and rank make him proud. Men competed to join him from a country several thousand li around, and three thousand retainers ate at his gate. Once, while he and the king were playing a board game, beacons flared on the northern frontier: "Zhao raiders are crossing the border." The king put down the game and wanted to summon his ministers. Before long word came from the north that it had indeed been a hunt. "How did you know?" the king asked. A retainer of mine, Wuji said, has a way of learning the king of Zhao's private business and reports it to me. From then on, the Records says, the king "dreaded the prince's ability, and did not dare entrust him with affairs of state."

edits_applied.before: King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that Wuji had seized the army on a forged order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan and proposed to enfeoff him with five cities. One reading is that this closing episode writes Wuji's survival and Wei's survival on the same line.

英文已削到中文范围：删去 the ruins of Daliang、城之東門、天下諸公子喜士、魏王泣迎授上将軍印、蒙骜、函谷關、万斤金、毁谤原话、醇酒妇女、初置东郡、屠大梁等中文没有的事实与数字，只保留中文所有的留赵十年、劝归、率五国破秦、重金毁谤、代将、谢病饮酒四年而死、死后秦攻魏拔二十城、十八年后虏魏王，并与R9修改后的中文一致。

issues.problem: 「门客里有一位侯嬴」把侯嬴的身份提前了：证据中他当时是魏国隐士、大梁夷门监者（E4），是无忌去请的人，直到宴罢才「侯生遂為上客」（E38），并非门客之一。
issues.suggestion: 改为「魏国有位隐士侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门」，「宴罢，侯嬴成为上客」保留。

issues.problem: 「话也越说越重」暗示使者多次传话、语气递进；证据只记平原君使者一次责让之辞（E11：讓魏公子曰），无渐次加重的记载。
issues.suggestion: 删「也越说越重」，改为「使者代平原君责让无忌，话说得很重」。

issues.problem: 「赵王因他一再辞让」中的「一再」无据，原文只写「以公子退讓也」（一次侧行辞让、自言罪过）（E31）。
issues.suggestion: 删「一再」，作「赵王因他辞让，口不忍献五城」。

issues.problem: 「后来赵王以主人之礼相迎」把E31的「趙王埽除自迎，執主人之禮」写成E23边界迎接之后的另一次场合；两处很可能是同一迎接事件的详略两种记述，分开写易让读者以为有两次迎接。
issues.suggestion: 删「后来」，并入上一段迎接场景或写「迎接时赵王执主人之礼」。

issues.problem: 说侯嬴自刭的动机「没有更多交代」与证据矛盾：E20有侯生自述动机「北鄉自剄，以送公子」。
issues.suggestion: 改为「侯嬴自刭除自述『以送公子』外再无交代；如姬盗符之后的下落，原文没有记载」。

issues.problem: 引述毛公、薛公之语时写成「诸侯之所以敬重他，『徒以有魏也』」，原文是「公子所以重於趙，名聞諸侯者，徒以有魏也」，兼说「被赵国看重」与「名闻诸侯」，稿件只留下「诸侯敬重」一层。
issues.suggestion: 改为「毛公、薛公说他『所以重於趙，名聞諸侯者，徒以有魏也』」。

issues.problem: 「褒扬落在他敬重侯嬴这一端」把太史公「信陵君之接岩穴隱者，不恥下交」（E37）限定为侯嬴一人；该评语涵盖岩穴隐者（侯嬴与毛公、薛公皆是，见E36），且E37明说他求问夷门、高祖奉祠，褒扬不止于侯嬴一事。
issues.suggestion: 改为「褒扬落在他结交岩穴隐者、不耻下交这一端，而不在矫令杀将上」。

issues.problem: 引「始吾聞平原君賢，故負魏王而救趙」是节引，原文下句还有「以稱平原君」；译作「以为平原君贤明，才辜负魏王去救赵」把动机只归于「以为他贤明」，漏了「以成全平原君」这层。
issues.suggestion: 补一句「以成全平原君」，或标明是节引。

review_after.overall: 稿件与证据包高度一致，日期数字、引语、人物称谓基本准确，无硬伤；仅侯嬴身份提前、个别节引与译法偏差、以及「一再」「越说越重」等少量无据修饰需修改。

issues.problem: The Chinese labels this as the author's own inference (「作者推断」), but the English opens with "One reading:", which turns an attributed judgment into an anonymous possible reading and also makes the sentence read as if the reading itself is the mistake.
issues.suggestion: Restore the attribution: "The author's inference: treating this as a friend staking everything for a friend would miss where the real difficulty lay."

issues.problem: The English adds many facts that are not in the Chinese: Master Mao living among gamblers and Master Xue among ale-sellers, the king of Wei meeting Wuji in tears and giving him the seal of supreme commander, the rout "beyond the river", the general Meng Ao, the pursuit to the Hangu Pass, "ten thousand jin of gold", the content of the slander (exile ten years / they want to make him king) and that the king heard it daily, "set up its first commandery there", and "put Daliang to the sword"; the Chinese only has 重金, 破秦, 拔二十城, 俘虏了魏王.
issues.suggestion: Trim these additions from the English (keep "much gold", "routed Qin", "took twenty cities", "captured the king of Wei"), or add the same details to the Chinese.

issues.problem: 「畏公子之賢能」 (feared the prince's worth and ability) is rendered "dreaded the prince's ability", dropping the 賢 / moral worth half of the phrase.
issues.suggestion: Use "dreaded the prince's worth and ability".

parity_after.overall: The English tracks the Chinese closely on facts, names, numbers, dates and quotations; the only substantive divergence is one section that over-translates with details absent from the Chinese, plus a dropped author attribution and one dropped word.
